newsitem.title: UK: Accord faces overhaul by B.Gas, NGC.
newsitem.headline: Accord faces overhaul by B.Gas, NGC.

text.p: Accord Energy Ltd, the energy marketing and trading company jointly owned by British Gas Plc and NGC Corp of Houston, is to undergo a major restructuring, NGC said in a statement on Wednesday.
Under the new plans, NGC will be able "to more effectively pursue its core business in the United Kingdom". Through NGC UK Ltd, it will assume control of Accord's crude oil business.

And NGC will also develop in the UK and Europe its "Energy Store" concept, already developed in the U.S., through which it will market gas liquids, crude oil, oil products, electricity, Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) and financial services as well as natural gas.
Accord will continue with its own core business of marketing natural gas, of which it sold 600 million cubic feet per day in the first nine months of 1996.

NGC said that the restructuring of Accord is related to the proposed demerger of British Gas, and the consequent creation of two new companies -- Centrica Plc and BG Plc -- which will go ahead if approved at a shareholder meeting on February 12.
Assuming the demerger gets approval, Centrica will take over operating control and maintain 51 percent ownership of Accord while NGC continues to own 49 percent of the company.
British Gas currently owns 26 percent of NGC.

The managing director of NGC UK will be Ian Wybrew-Bond, formerly Director of Shell International Gas Ltd and Head of Business Development, Western Europe. He will join NGC on March 1. Other senior officials will be Gary Cardone, director, UK Trading; Deborah Chance, director, European Marketing; and Mike Fulwood, director, Finance.

NGC Chairman and CEO Chuck Watson said in a statement: "This agreement, which allows NGC to replicate in the UK and Europe the successful Energy Store concept we've built in North America, sets the stage for the growth of the company throughout Europe and around the globe. As the European gas industry continues to evolve, we believe that our concept of multi-fuel commodity marketing will play a critical role in the future success of the European energy market."
